topic.reason: הנושא נקבע בתוכנית השבועית (חבילה 5 מתוך 7, כל חבילה על נושא אחר). כיבוי מסך הוא רגע של כל ערב ואין כאן טענה על תאריך. יש עליו מקורות טובים שנקראו היום: האקדמיה האמריקאית לרפואת ילדים (עמוד של ד״ר ג׳ני רדסקי), מחקר של אוניברסיטת וושינגטון על 28 משפחות, Common Sense Media בשיתוף Child Mind Institute ו-The Conversation. בקטלוג אין ספר על מסכים, אבל באתר אפשר ליצור סיפור חדש, ויש את הדובי משנה צבעים (גילאי 2 עד 6) על זיהוי רגשות כמו כעס, לקישור בהודעה.

voice.note: קול מכויל: 37 דוגמאות מאושרות מתוך העריכות של ירין. הכתיבה לפי שינויי העריכה האחרונים (דוגמה אחת בשקופית כשאפשר, סיכום קצר בלי רשימת נקודות).

sources.title: Screen Time & Temper Tantrums: Helpful Tips for Parents
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org, American Academy of Pediatrics (by Jenny Radesky, MD, FAAP; last updated 3/13/2024)
sources.quote: Difficulty switching gears does not automatically mean your child is hopelessly hooked on tech. ... Toddlers and younger school-aged children are still learning to deal with anger, frustration and disappointment. ... This isn't the time to go over the rules, since a child in meltdown mode can't think logically. Simply hold your ground, using as few words as possible: "I know it's tough, but it's time to put your tablet away." ... Pausing before speaking or acting can help you maintain the calm you need to help your child. ... Kids can benefit from having a spot where they can go to calm down. ... If your child starts to rage when screen time ends, ask them to go to their quiet spot until they feel better. If necessary, gently pick up a younger child or lead them by the hand. Tell them you'll be glad to see them again when they're ready to reconnect. ... researchers found that tossing a pillow in the air and challenging kids to bat it in a new direction helped work off momentary tension. ... Try it with younger kids, too: offer a beloved book, cuddle time with the family pet or a small chore that makes them feel part of the group. ... If you've found warnings are useful for your child, consider using a timer they set themselves. This models the idea of self-regulation and helps kids feel more in control.
sources.supports: Difficulty switching gears does not automatically mean a child is hooked; young children are still learning to deal with disappointment; few words and holding your ground; pausing to stay calm; a quiet spot and coming back when ready; tossing a pillow to bat; trading up to a pet cuddle or a small chore; a timer the child sets. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

sources.title: How do I put a stop to screen time (turn off the TV or take the phone away) without causing a meltdown?
sources.publisher: Common Sense Media (the Child Mind Institute contributed; last reviewed or updated September 27, 2021)
sources.quote: A lot of parents worry that a tantrum means a child has developed an unhealthy attachment to the phone or tablet, but that's very unlikely. ... Turn it off and stick to your guns.
sources.supports: Parents often worry that a tantrum over a tablet means an unhealthy attachment, which the page calls very unlikely; turn it off and stick to your guns. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

sources.title: Two-minute warnings make kids’ ‘screen time’ tantrums worse
sources.publisher: UW News, University of Washington (Jennifer Langston, May 5, 2016; on Hiniker, Suh, Cao and Kientz, CHI 2016)
sources.quote: “The kids we looked at for this particular study are right in that power struggle age,” Kientz said. “It’s much easier to do that with a person than with technology. Once you take that parental withholding component out of it, kids are a lot more accepting.” ... Screen time transitions also went more smoothly if the technology was to blame.
sources.supports: Children in the power struggle age accept the end more easily from technology than from a parent; transitions went more smoothly when the technology was to blame. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

claims.wording_he: אני לא מכורה למסך עוד קשה לי להפסיק
claims.supports: AAP: difficulty switching gears does not automatically mean your child is hopelessly hooked on tech; Common Sense Media: worrying that a tantrum means an unhealthy attachment is common, but that is very unlikely. The page also says to see the pediatrician if meltdowns happen nearly every time; we do not claim more than 'not automatically'.

claims.supports: AAP: toddlers and younger school-aged children are still learning to deal with anger, frustration and disappointment.

claims.wording_he: משפט אחד קצר והטאבלט לא חוזר
claims.supports: AAP: hold your ground with as few words as possible ('I know it's tough, but it's time to put your tablet away'); Common Sense Media: stick to your guns.
AAP: parents need to avoid having a tantrum too; a few deep breaths and pausing before speaking help keep the calm needed to help the child.
AAP: a spot to calm down; for physical acting out, tossing a pillow in the air for the child to bat helped work off tension.
AAP: tell them you'll be glad to see them again when they're ready to reconnect.

claims.wording_he: חיבוק עם החתול או משימה קטנה איתך
claims.supports: AAP 'trading up': cuddle time with the family pet or a small chore that makes them feel part of the group.
AAP: a timer they set themselves helps kids feel more in control; UW: kids accept the end more easily when the parental withholding is taken out of it ('זה לא את נגדי' is our wording).
